_comment: Baseline allowlist for TC-COMPLIANCE.RFC-01 (`cargo xtask cache-tests`).
Every entry is a cache-tests test of kind `required` that fixture-proxy
does not pass, together with the reason it is NOT attributable to this
crate's Storage backend. Since pingora-cache does not itself claim full
RFC 9111 conformance, a required failure of this backend is checked
against the behaviour of pingora-cache itself before it is attributed to
this backend; this file records the outcome of that triage.
Every reason below was verified by reading the pingora-cache 0.8.1
source, not inferred from the failure text. Citations are file:line in
the pinned crate. A NEW required failure not listed here fails the
command -- that is the actual regression signal this baseline exists to
Tests of kind `optimal` and `check` are informational by cache-tests'
check -> yes/no observation) and are reported but never gate the run.
A reason beginning `FLAKY:` marks a test observed landing both ways
across runs. Those are exempt from the 'this baselined test now passes,
remove it' notice, since a passing run does not make the entry stale.

2026-09-15: partial-use-headers and partial-use-stored-headers were removed from this allowlist. Both failed only because the backend did not advertise HandleHit::can_seek, so pingora-cache served a full 200 instead of assembling a 206; SDS-LAYOUT.OBJECTFILE-01 now requires seek support on a published record, and both tests pass.

allowed_required_failures.304-etag-update-response-Content-Foo: pingora-cache merges only a fixed 5-header allowlist from a 304 (cache-control, expires, cache-tag, cdn-cache-control, etag) rather than RFC 9111 4.3.4's 'update its header fields with the header fields provided in the 304' -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1096 revalidate_merge_header. Arbitrary headers are never merged, upstream of Storage entirely: the backend persists verbatim whatever CacheMeta update_meta is handed (proven by compat_validators.rs / compat_freshness.rs).
allowed_required_failures.304-etag-update-response-Test-Header: Same fixed 304 merge allowlist -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1096 revalidate_merge_header.
allowed_required_failures.304-etag-update-response-X-Content-Foo: Same fixed 304 merge allowlist -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1096 revalidate_merge_header.
allowed_required_failures.304-etag-update-response-X-Test-Header: Same fixed 304 merge allowlist -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1096 revalidate_merge_header.
allowed_required_failures.age-parse-large: pingora-cache never reads the Age header when computing freshness: filters::calculate_fresh_until consults Cache-Control, then Expires, then CacheMetaDefaults, and nothing else (pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72). A stored response's apparent age from the origin is therefore not an input to staleness at all.
allowed_required_failures.age-parse-large-minus-one: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.age-parse-larger: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.age-parse-suffix: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.age-parse-suffix-twoline: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.freshness-expires-age-fast-date: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.freshness-expires-age-slow-date: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.freshness-max-age-age: Age not an input to freshness -- pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:72 calculate_fresh_until.
allowed_required_failures.freshness-expires-old-date: pingora-cache computes fresh_until from Expires as an absolute instant (filters::calculate_expires_header_time, pingora-cache/src/filters.rs:120) without reconciling it against the origin's Date header, so an intentionally-skewed Date does not shift freshness.
allowed_required_failures.cdn-fresh-cc-nostore: pingora-cache implements no CDN-Cache-Control semantics. The header name appears exactly once in the whole crate, in the 304 merge allowlist (pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1111) -- i.e. it is copied through, never interpreted as a caching directive.
allowed_required_failures.cdn-max-age-0-expires: CDN-Cache-Control not interpreted -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1111 (copied, never parsed).
allowed_required_failures.cdn-max-age-long-cc-max-age: CDN-Cache-Control not interpreted -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1111 (copied, never parsed).
allowed_required_failures.cdn-no-cache: CDN-Cache-Control not interpreted -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1111 (copied, never parsed).
allowed_required_failures.cdn-no-store-cc-fresh: CDN-Cache-Control not interpreted -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1111 (copied, never parsed).
allowed_required_failures.cdn-private: CDN-Cache-Control not interpreted -- pingora-cache/src/lib.rs:1111 (copied, never parsed).
allowed_required_failures.invalidate-DELETE: pingora-cache invalidates only on an explicit purge request from the proxy application; it does not invalidate on unsafe request methods, leaving that RFC 9111 4.4 duty to the application. This is stated as a scope boundary in FRE-COMPLIANCE.PURGE-01's own text, and confirmed in source: no Method::{POST,PUT,DELETE} handling exists anywhere in pingora-cache.
allowed_required_failures.invalidate-M-SEARCH: No unsafe-method invalidation in pingora-cache -- see FRE-COMPLIANCE.PURGE-01's scope note.
allowed_required_failures.invalidate-POST: No unsafe-method invalidation in pingora-cache -- see FRE-COMPLIANCE.PURGE-01's scope note.
allowed_required_failures.invalidate-PUT: No unsafe-method invalidation in pingora-cache -- see FRE-COMPLIANCE.PURGE-01's scope note.
allowed_required_failures.other-age-update-expires: Age generation on a served hit is computed by pingora-cache itself, by CacheMeta::age() (pingora-cache/src/meta.rs:517), measured from the stored epoch/updated instant. The backend round-trips those instants exactly (proven by compat_freshness.rs); what the test observes is the Age arithmetic pingora-cache chooses after a revalidation, upstream of Storage.
allowed_required_failures.other-age-update-max-age: Age arithmetic after revalidation is done by pingora-cache -- pingora-cache/src/meta.rs:517 CacheMeta::age().
allowed_required_failures.other-date-update: Date on a served hit is regenerated by the proxy rather than replayed from the stored response head. The backend returns the stored Date byte-exactly (proven by compat_headers.rs); the served value is chosen above the Storage boundary.
allowed_required_failures.other-date-update-expires: Date regenerated by the proxy, not replayed from storage -- see other-date-update.
allowed_required_failures.headers-omit-headers-listed-in-Connectio: Stripping hop-by-hop headers named in Connection is a proxy/protocol-layer duty (RFC 9110 7.6.1), performed before any caching decision. Nothing about it reaches the Storage trait.
allowed_required_failures.interim-not-cached: FLAKY: lands both ways, always with 'Interim response 1 not received'. Root-caused 2026-09-23 and fixed: pingora-proxy drops an already-filtered downstream batch when the cache takes over part-way through it (proxy_h1.rs, h1_response_filter_and_send), so a 1xx batched with the final response head is discarded. This backend used to make that batching the norm by running its file I/O on the service worker, of which Pingora gives each service one by default; ADR-STORAGE.EXECUTOR-01 moved it to the blocking pool. Measured before and after on one worker under load, at a 0.3 ms origin gap: 10/40 interims survived before, 38/40 after, against MemCache's 40/40. What remains is the batching bug in Pingora itself, which both backends share equally, so this entry stays as a FLAKY: record rather than an attribution to this crate.
allowed_required_failures.stale-while-revalidate-window: Enforcing the stale-while-revalidate window is the serve-stale decision of pingora-cache (CacheMeta::serve_stale_while_revalidate, pingora-cache/src/meta.rs:538). The backend round-trips the stale_while_revalidate_sec value exactly (proven by compat_freshness.rs's stale-overflow-cap scenario); when to honour it is decided above the Storage boundary.
